chunks: And in another report, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him)

regarding the Word of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'Spend from the good things that you earn,' so he said: 'The people had earned evil earnings during the Pre-Islamic period. So when they became Muslims, they wanted to take these out from their wealth in order to give charity with it. So, Allah, Blessed and High, Refused except that they should take out from the good of what they had been earning.'
ai.seo_question: Why did Allah specify spending from 'good things' rather than all wealth?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi offers a specific exegetical context (asbab al-nuzul) for Surah Al-Baqarah 2:267, clarifying that the command to spend from 'good things' was a refinement for early Muslims who wished to donate all their wealth, including that acquired through questionable means during the Jahiliyyah. It highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the qualitative purity (tayyib) of wealth rather than mere quantity, distinguishing between the general accumulation of assets and the spiritual merit of the portion given in charity.
